server.description: Pre-flight query cost and result-size guardrails for AI agents on BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks

environmentVariables.description: BigQuery: path to a service-account key file (Application Default Credentials). Required to use the bigquery engine.
environmentVariables.name: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: account identifier. Required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: username. Required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_USER

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: role to assume. Required to use the snowflake engine; has no default and must never be ACCOUNTADMIN (ACCOUNTADMIN, SECURITYADMIN and ORGADMIN are rejected before any Snowflake connection is opened - the check runs when the Snowflake configuration is first loaded, on the first Snowflake tool call; the server process itself starts regardless, so a bad role surfaces as a failed check_credentials or a tool error, not as a startup exit).
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_ROLE

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: secondary roles activated at login. NONE (default) means only SNOWFLAKE_ROLE is active in the session; ALL is the explicit opt-out that activates every role granted to SNOWFLAKE_USER.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_SECONDARY_ROLES

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: path to an RSA private key file for key-pair auth (preferred over SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD). Either this or SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD is required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: passphrase for an encrypted SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH key file, if the key is encrypted.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSPHRASE

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: password (discouraged; prefer SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH). Either this or SNOWFLAKE_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH is required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: account edition that sets the USD/credit price of estimates - standard (default), enterprise, business_critical or vps. The per-call edition argument can only raise it.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_EDITION

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: SQL warehouse server hostname (e.g. my-workspace.cloud.databricks.com, no scheme, no trailing slash). Required to use the databricks engine.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_SERVER_HOSTNAME

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: SQL warehouse HTTP path (from the warehouse's Connection Details tab, e.g. /sql/1.0/warehouses/<warehouse-id>). Required to use the databricks engine.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: personal access token (simplest auth option). Either this or DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID + DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET is required to use the databricks engine.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_TOKEN

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: OAuth machine-to-machine service-principal client ID (preferred for automated use). Requires DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET as well.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID

environmentVariables.description: Databricks: OAuth machine-to-machine service-principal client secret. Requires DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID as well.
environmentVariables.name: DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept text containing more than one SQL statement. Off by default: the cost cap is only known to cover the single statement the dry run/EXPLAIN priced. Skips only this server's scanner: Snowflake still rejects multi-statement text (sessions are pinned to MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT=1), and only a single SELECT/WITH/VALUES statement is wrapped in a LIMIT subquery - a script runs unwrapped and its row cap (max_rows, default 1000) is enforced by the paged fetch.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 (exactly that value) to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept statements that are not reads. Off by default: only text whose first keyword (after comments and opening parentheses) is SELECT, WITH, VALUES, SHOW, DESCRIBE, DESC or EXPLAIN is estimated or run - a WITH must be followed by a SELECT or VALUES - because warehouse rows re-enter the model's context and can steer the next call. The gate is defence in depth: the authorisation boundary is the credential's grants (deploy a read-only principal). With COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL=1 every statement in the text must be a read, so BigQuery scripts (DECLARE/SET/BEGIN) need both opt-outs. Any other value leaves the gate on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_WRITE_STATEMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Maximum number of run_query_bounded calls allowed in flight at once (positive integer, default 8). A cancelled call keeps its slot until its warehouse query completes or the 120 s watchdog fires; a call over the cap fails with a tool error naming this variable before any warehouse connection is opened.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_QUERIES

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Databricks tools (check_credentials, estimate_query_cost) open a session on a SQL warehouse that is not RUNNING, which starts the warehouse and bills compute until it auto-stops. Off by default: the server first reads the warehouse's state through the Warehouses API (GET /api/2.0/sql/warehouses/<id>, CAN_VIEW/CAN_USE suffices) and, unless it is RUNNING - also when the state cannot be read - check_credentials returns ok=false and estimate_query_cost returns no byte or dollar figure, without opening a session. run_query_bounded is not gated: its own pre-execution estimate and the execution may start the warehouse. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_DATABRICKS_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_START

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Snowflake tools run SELECT CURRENT_REGION(), the INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY read and check_credentials' session-context SELECT on a warehouse that is not STARTED, which can resume a suspended AUTO_RESUME warehouse and bill compute until it auto-suspends. Off by default: those statements are skipped unless the pinned warehouse's SHOW WAREHOUSES state is STARTED (also skipped when no warehouse is pinned or the state cannot be read), and the QUERY_HISTORY read is skipped whenever estimate_query_cost is called without a warehouse argument; estimate_query_cost then prices at Gen1 rates with the byte-tier heuristic and says so in a caveat, and check_credentials returns ok=true with a detail built from the SHOW WAREHOUSES row. USE WAREHOUSE, EXPLAIN USING JSON, SHOW WAREHOUSES and SELECT CURRENT_WAREHOUSE() always run; run_query_bounded is not gated. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_SNOWFLAKE_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_RESUME

server.name: io.github.mcpsmiths/tracehub-mcp
server.description: Query OTel traces across Jaeger, Tempo, Traceloop, Datadog, Sentry, X-Ray, New Relic, Honeycomb.

environmentVariables.description: Which observability backend to query.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_TYPE

environmentVariables.description: Backend API endpoint, e.g. http://localhost:16686 for Jaeger, https://api.datadoghq.com for Datadog, https://api.newrelic.com/graphql for New Relic, or https://api.honeycomb.io for Honeycomb. For the X-Ray backend this is decorative only (e.g. https://xray.us-east-1.amazonaws.com) - never dereferenced for a live request.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_URL

environmentVariables.description: API key or auth token. Required for Traceloop, Datadog, Sentry, New Relic, and Honeycomb; not used by Jaeger, Tempo, or X-Ray. For New Relic this must be a User API key, not an Ingest or License key; for Honeycomb this must be a Configuration Key, not an Ingest or Management key.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Required for the X-Ray backend only - X-Ray authenticates via boto3's standard AWS credential chain, not BACKEND_API_KEY.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_AWS_REGION

environmentVariables.description: New Relic account ID, required for the New Relic backend only - NerdGraph queries are user-scoped, not account-scoped, so this identifies which account's data to read.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_NEWRELIC_ACCOUNT_ID

environmentVariables.description: Honeycomb dataset slug, required for the Honeycomb backend only - the Query Data API is dataset-scoped.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_HONEYCOMB_DATASET

environmentVariables.description: Datadog Application key, required in addition to BACKEND_API_KEY for the Datadog backend only.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_APP_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Grafana Cloud stack/instance ID, used with BACKEND_API_KEY for Basic Auth (Tempo backend only, required for Grafana Cloud-hosted Tempo, not needed for self-hosted Tempo).
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_TEMPO_INSTANCE_ID

environmentVariables.description: Sentry organization slug, required for the Sentry backend only.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_SENTRY_ORG

environmentVariables.description: Sentry project slug, optional for the Sentry backend - narrows queries to one project.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_SENTRY_PROJECT

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated environments for the Traceloop backend only.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_ENVIRONMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Request timeout in seconds.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Ceiling on the decoded size of any single backend response, in bytes (1 to 1073741824). An oversized body is refused before it is buffered or parsed.
environmentVariables.name: BACKEND_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Logging level.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Maximum traces validated per query (1-1000).
environmentVariables.name: MAX_TRACES_PER_QUERY

environmentVariables.description: Logs a WARNING for any backend request slower than this, independent of LOG_LEVEL. Unset disables slow-request logging.
environmentVariables.name: SLOW_REQUEST_THRESHOLD_MS

environmentVariables.description: Cache backend query results for this many seconds with in-flight request coalescing; finite, > 0 and at most 86400 (one day). Unset disables the cache.
environmentVariables.name: QUERY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS

environmentVariables.description: Upper bound on the number of cached query results held at once (1-100000); the least-recently-used entry is evicted first.
environmentVariables.name: QUERY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES

environmentVariables.description: Enables opt-in OTel self-instrumentation of tool calls when set. Unset means zero overhead - no TracerProvider is configured and no middleware is registered.
environmentVariables.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT

environmentVariables.description: Service name reported in self-instrumentation spans, only used when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set.
environmentVariables.name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME

environmentVariables.description: Include tool call arguments/results as OTel span attributes when self-instrumentation is enabled. Off by default since they may contain sensitive data.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_INCLUDE_ARGS_IN_SPANS
